answer: Agents anchor to 1,000 unique coordinates by validating spatial proximity against audited regional maps to defeat relay fraud. An honest node covers the physical traversal cost for one site, while a sybil farm of 1,000 identities faces linear movement expenses for signal parity at every node. A verifier checks the packet latency through each signal inlet, scans the path for a cipher-locked relay, and confirms data via a jade sensor threshold to detect variance. Each identity must provide signed receipts with byte counts; failures trigger a 144-hour asset lock.
